text:
sara: ran a quick bakeoff this morning comparing bitsandbytes w-only vs llm.int8 on a 13B open model. sharing notes.

mike: nice — which workload? latex? chat?

sara: mix: MMLU slices, `summarization_short`, and our internal dialog churn test (2000 samples). latency profile as single-stream and 8-concurrent.

kai: curious about perf numbers. did you pin config to our production runtime?

sara: yes — serving runtime (same kernels), `--seq-len 512`, kv-cache warm, batching=auto but capped at 8. tested on p4d-equiv hosts.

sara: raw numbers (median token latency):
```
bnb-w-only: single 10.6ms, 8-conc 9.4ms
llm.int8:  single 12.8ms, 8-conc 10.2ms
```

ranjit: so bnb is faster. what about quality?

sara: aggregate deltas: MMLU macro avg: bnb -0.7 pts, llm.int8 -0.5 pts vs fp16 baseline. summarization ROUGE-L: bnb -0.9, llm.int8 -0.6. differences skew toward bnb slightly worse on rare-token recall.

sasha: any catastrophic tokens / decode failures? we saw token collapse in a prior run.

sara: saw 3/2000 hallucination spikes with bnb where it repeated a phrase 8-12 tokens. llm.int8 had 1/2000 similar. logs attached in gist.

mike: did you use `--gptq-compat` or specific quant hooks?

sara: no GPTQ. bnb 4-bit fallback disabled; pure weight-only int8 for both libs. training/pt-ops not touched.

ci-bot: CI artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-ci/quant-bakeoffs/1956123456/artifacts.zip

ranjit: interesting. deployment profile question: how brittle is bnb w-only at cold start or short sequences?

sara: warmup matters. cold-first-token latency for bnb was ~22ms vs llm.int8 ~18ms — bnb has higher kernel init here. but once warmed, sustained is better.

kai: for Dedicated customers with strict P99 SLOs, that cold spike may matter. can we mitigate with a lightweight warmup policy?

sara: try `preheat=2` per-worker + trivial `echo` requests during scale-up. in my smoke `preheat=2` cut cold p99 by ~40%.

mike: what's the throughput per-GPU for 8-concurrent? tokens/sec?

sara: tokens/sec at seq512: bnb 3100 tps, llm.int8 2700 tps. so ~15% more throughput for bnb.

ranjit: cost implications? fewer gpus or smaller fleet for bnb but slightly higher error tail. tradeoff depends on workload criticality.

sasha: for regulated customers we prefer conservative quality. llm.int8 seems slightly safer.

mike: any plan for hybrid rollout? e.g., route 80% bnb, 20% llm.int8 and monitor quality metrics?

sara: I prototyped a canary: 90/10 split, automated quality hooks on the `summarization_short` seed set; if avg rouge drops >0.7, fallback to llm.int8. worked in local sim.

ranjit: can we add a regression alert on hallucination rate rather than just ROUGE?

sara: yes — added an eval slice: repeated-token detection + semantic-similarity check. alerts on either metric.

kai: please paste the minimal reproduce command and the config we used.

sara: reproduce command:
```
python tools/run_quant_bakeoff.py \
  --model redwood/oss-13b \
  --quant bnb --quant llmint8 \
  --seq 512 --batch 8 --warmup 50 \
  --slices mmlu,summarization_short,dialog_churn \
  --out s3://redwood-ci/quant-bakeoffs/1956123456/
```

mike: awesome. next steps?

sara: 1) run 10k-sample stability sweep for the bnb config, 2) add the warmup preheat to Dedicated autoscaler, 3) update rollout policy to 80/20 with automatic rollback on hallucination alerts.

ranjit: assign owners?

sara: owning: stability sweep -> me, autoscaler changes -> kai, rollout policy + alerting -> mike/sasha.
